questions.question: Which singer released the hit song Shake It Off in 2014?
questions.explanation: Shake It Off was the first single from Taylor Swift's album 1989, named after the year she was born.

questions.question: Which British singer named his albums after maths symbols, such as plus, multiply and divide?
questions.explanation: Ed Sheeran's albums include + (Plus), x (Multiply), ÷ (Divide) and = (Equals).

questions.question: Which England footballer campaigned in 2020 for children to get free school meals in the holidays?
questions.explanation: Marcus Rashford remembered relying on free school meals himself as a boy in Manchester.

questions.question: Ant and Dec have presented which ITV show set in the Australian jungle?
options: I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here!
questions.answer: I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here!
questions.explanation: Ant and Dec first presented I'm a Celebrity in 2002, when it began.

questions.question: The YouTuber DanTDM became famous for videos about which game?
questions.explanation: The TDM in his name stands for The Diamond Minecart.

questions.question: Which sprinter ran 100 metres in just 9.58 seconds in 2009?
questions.explanation: Usain Bolt set that time at the World Championships in Berlin, and he liked to celebrate with his famous lightning-bolt pose.

questions.question: Which girl group became the first group ever to win The X Factor, in 2011?
questions.explanation: Perrie, Jade, Jesy and Leigh-Anne's first single was a cover of the song 'Cannonball'.

questions.question: Which famous naturalist narrated Blue Planet II in 2017?
questions.explanation: Blue Planet II made so many viewers worry about plastic in the sea that people talk about the Blue Planet effect.

questions.question: Which fitness coach became known as 'the nation's PE teacher' for his live YouTube workouts during the 2020 lockdown?
questions.explanation: His PE with Joe sessions went out every weekday morning, and earned him a Guinness World Record and an MBE.

questions.question: Which swimmer won 23 Olympic gold medals between 2004 and 2016?
questions.explanation: Michael Phelps won eight of them at a single Games, in Beijing in 2008.

questions.question: Which Olympic champion diver is also famous for knitting at the poolside?
questions.explanation: Tom Daley knitted a cardigan with Olympic rings on it during the Tokyo Games.

questions.question: Who is the voice of Elsa, singing Let It Go in Frozen?
questions.explanation: Kristen Bell is the voice of Anna, and Idina Menzel sings as her sister Elsa.

questions.question: Which baker judged the very first series of The Great British Bake Off, in 2010, alongside Mary Berry?
questions.explanation: Paul Hollywood's firm handshake became one of the most wanted prizes in the tent.

questions.question: Which YouTuber, whose real name is Jimmy Donaldson, is famous for giant challenges and giveaways?
questions.explanation: MrBeast started posting videos as a teenager in North Carolina in 2012.

questions.question: Who captained England's Lionesses when they won the European Championship in 2022?
questions.explanation: Leah Williamson lifted the trophy at Wembley after England beat Germany 2-1 in the final.

questions.question: Which singer was born Stefani Germanotta?
questions.explanation: Her stage name is said to come from the Queen song Radio Ga Ga.

questions.question: Which member of Queen wrote Bohemian Rhapsody?
questions.explanation: Released in 1975, it spent nine weeks at number one in the UK despite being almost six minutes long.

questions.question: Who presented the first series of Strictly Come Dancing in 2004, alongside Tess Daly?
questions.explanation: Sir Bruce hosted the main show for ten years, with his catchphrase Nice to see you, to see you nice.

questions.question: Which former Take That singer had a huge solo hit with 'Angels' in 1997?
questions.explanation: His three concerts at Knebworth in 2003 drew around 375,000 fans, about 125,000 a night.

questions.question: Which singer was born Reginald Dwight?
questions.explanation: He grew up in Pinner, north-west London, and changed his name officially in 1972.

questions.question: Which fiery chef tried to rescue struggling restaurants on the TV show Kitchen Nightmares?
questions.explanation: Before he became a chef he played youth football for Rangers, until a knee injury ended his hopes.

questions.question: Who presented Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? in the UK from 1998 to 2014?
questions.explanation: Chris Tarrant made the question Is that your final answer? a national catchphrase.

questions.question: Who co-wrote Gavin and Stacey with James Corden and played Nessa?
questions.explanation: The pair came up with it after meeting while acting in the ITV drama Fat Friends.

questions.question: Which former England striker presented Match of the Day from 1999 to 2025?
questions.explanation: He won the Golden Boot at the 1986 World Cup and was never shown a yellow or red card in his whole career.

questions.question: Who became the first man to win three Best Actor Oscars, the third in 2013 for Lincoln?
questions.explanation: His other two Best Actor wins were for My Left Foot and There Will Be Blood.

questions.question: Which singer released the album Guts in 2023?
questions.explanation: Guts followed her first album, Sour, which included the hit drivers license.

questions.question: Who sang the theme song for the James Bond film No Time to Die?
questions.explanation: She was still a teenager when she recorded it, the youngest singer ever to record a Bond theme.

questions.question: Which chef led a 2005 TV campaign to improve school dinners?
questions.explanation: Jamie's School Dinners famously took on the Turkey Twizzler.

questions.question: Which golfer won the Masters in 2025 to complete his career Grand Slam?
questions.explanation: Rory McIlroy beat Justin Rose in a play-off at Augusta to win all four of golf's major titles.

questions.question: Which DJ presented the very first show on BBC Radio 1, in 1967?
questions.explanation: Tony Blackburn opened the station on 30 September 1967, and the first full record he played was Flowers in the Rain by The Move.
